name: Cuba
summary: Spain’s long-held colony, then an independence constrained by U.S. intervention.
notes: The British held Havana and western districts in 1762–1763, not all Cuba. Guantánamo Bay’s lease is not an island-wide transfer. The 1959 revolution changed the government, not Cuba’s sovereign independence.

events.title: Spain claims Cuba
events.detail: Columbus’s voyage reached Cuba; colonization followed later.
events.qualification: A European claim; it does not establish island-wide administration or extinguish Indigenous rights.

events.title: Spanish conquest begins
events.detail: Diego Velázquez established a colony and launched the conquest of Indigenous communities.

events.title: Britain captures Havana
events.detail: British forces occupied Havana and nearby districts during the Seven Years’ War. Most of Cuba remained Spanish.

events.title: Havana returned to Spain
events.detail: The Treaty of Paris exchanged occupied Havana back to Spain; Spain ceded Florida to Britain.

events.title: Spain relinquishes sovereignty
events.detail: The Treaty of Paris ended Spain’s claim to Cuba. Unlike Puerto Rico, Cuba was not ceded to the United States.

events.title: U.S. military government
events.detail: Spanish colonial authority was replaced by an American military administration.

events.title: The Republic of Cuba takes office
events.detail: Occupation authority ended, but the Platt Amendment constrained independence by reserving a U.S. intervention right.

events.title: A second U.S. administration
events.detail: Domestic political crisis led to a U.S. provisional government.

events.title: Cuban government restored
events.detail: The provisional administration ended; American troops departed later that year.

events.title: Platt Amendment restrictions end
events.detail: A new treaty ended the general U.S. right of intervention; the Guantánamo lease continued.
